Friend, The fight for voting rights is taking place across the country right now. As elections approach, the Trump administration is taking steps to limit vote-by-mail and early voting, create approved voter lists in coordination with the Department of Homeland Security, and deploy federal troops to polling places. Already, several states have moved to further gerrymander congressional districts after key protections in the Voting Rights Act were weakened. **But there are still opportunities for everyday Americans to fight back.** **[That’s why we’re asking you to contribute $25 to the Voting Rights Fund today. The attacks on voting access are escalating, and we need the resources to fight back before these anti-democracy efforts become even more entrenched.](http://links.votingrightsfund.org/s/c/X6X4bXPg0-bwVjyQ2CajWNeJl3kphA002sv5Hk2Tm2hu622D5cmgzMCwNPGQMFirwKibddzZ6o0ctrQLjsTTGOFJ6TRlR-7uDudUofJ-d9FP7HkfvaacrUwlOaPQuFQfuLEeo9JEz3gp7MvFLmEfesj-zMly4ZX2trSRXrWVUOo7KA2sfGdH9lbzGX5Iq6phmW80dvLvY7Wrmr_CQwcoawBBWScch4-1W9npP_K5YTcgNEpA3qhU-KIBpSA6p0lQY_rXASVY3gnXroUSIOhJa3r74APCv53IrrELPcT7yvruOUwamsww4o29RmRUBKu2KrlZWXQWWQIt-x9YFYsXjAb-ywAAJmjRuLGRXsLFLHSUbCx9v9Ntgm8mwK-_y5H5jsGQrRV2Uyvsn5BdFLBM5GbNXC8AaAP055X7utMYs-_jcEfMf7qYMeQP_cSUuPtG-fsVnjNBPjxtlt3Vibz84OzNgLvygS1baJFX4rP2FCJs9CGRRUSn7GrXXP6-JUMgwKyAjj7s_tmWExAFO8ls61yVrmmGUazhUy9VoRwWobSYAjfWtG2M0j0KIGHsc19o58-h0oGpfErBWXKRZ0wM9uPVpsrXMiT4lQkZKDco8G5kLDI2B3P1evNX2wTSUY8X-o99lq3yo2tVgcjzF52yMnQ42yXbTfgrIR3wiM9Rpk6RHwOpozTZUFcWRM1luxBBen48ALchgz4mu16cEZpMe6BGNMKQZc5VwZzR--8SlSnfPpTQXQfmGw6q49B_wSj1VNq5TAasr7Ebmh94fVlnYUGbCDAPMTh_e_8XHdKRcfkP4mixz35ZQPGNpboAYCyPLV5h7roZyLp4hLbT467eoSZ7WCY5DHHDU5jCLMV7nWEEPxY71wpWKEPG8XIu1doRot0AOHOXXEO3u3E-r6fl5LxiCl3hqZn2r8uvN3kalMDltGnhEf7e/HiQv8K2He8J4ca5EL7sdtcj590PRpDEL/21)** In Arizona, one of the states most vulnerable to election denialism and election interference, a group of dedicated Americans has come together to enshrine new protections for voters. [The Protect the Vote Act](http://links.votingrightsfund.org/s/c/UhZHTQxbFl8dx_C923h_UCqD_HwWcBaRCEYaUBmKxrZZB1q81mUjJlFI9Xlm0UgcwXqgqPuV-4BIQNBgbohGiwvTlSIpNauxbcC2jJNx0ydiqAEexI82SN0pl-rw4CKKoGwFFiwfpgA9fWgshvajPO-sCFeBQcAO4B1oTGeWNtSMXmcjw1-1p422SlNMetG-jsYKOF9RBUzJ__7OwOJ6kJiJphLysa3a1Iy4HZgSlBakHTtatQEUGjVWLGqPNddNeKpk5WbdXqBCPQH1AKGgnPZJ-OnzRL3y_VpHoGVgujlpPxr7oomIFG9UB6pE0CoZqsTWFMDQelM1Cro2NKz3u9-JHyu5jQUi0ETq2skbTMYDEqc/WsSAhRn1MAQKet_o0xF64Wr9qxQP0nka/21) is a constitutional amendment that establishes a fundamental right to vote for every citizen. This system allowed eligible voters to automatically receive a ballot by mail for every election. I’ve spent my life fixing things that are broken.
On the factory floor.
In the Navy.
In the National Guard.
And right now, there’s nothing more broken than the United States Senate.
Washington isn’t working for people like us anymore. It’s working for billionaires, lobbyists, and corporations that write the rules for themselves — and leave the rest of us footing the bill.
I’m Dan Osborn, and I’m running for Senate to fix Washington. Please, chip in $10, $25, or whatever you can right now to help me → [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-osborn]
DONATE TODAY TO DEFEAT MAGA EXTREMISM! [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-osborn]
I’m not a career politician. I’m an industrial mechanic from Omaha, a former union leader who took on Kellogg’s to protect my coworkers’ wages and benefits, and a guy who knows what it means to work 80-hour weeks just to keep a middle-class life together.
And I’m running as an independent because I don’t owe either party a damn thing.
I owe you.
I’ll fight to cut taxes for working families, protect Social Security, stand up for family farms, and finally pass Right to Repair so corporations stop ripping people off just to fix what they own.
But I can’t do this alone. The same billionaires who broke Washington are going to spend whatever it takes to keep it that way.
So I’m asking: Will you chip in $10, $25, or anything you can right now to help us build a campaign that answers to working people — not the powerful? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-osborn]
Let's fix this.
—Dan Osborn

Here are the details on how Donald Trump -- while in Florida -- voted by mail and played golf instead of voting in-person ahead of a 2026 special election, straight from Politico:
" Trump requested his mail-in ballot on Saturday, March 14, according to public Palm Beach County voter records. The ballot was sent to Trump’s Mar-a-Lago estate the same day and was received for processing the next day, on Sunday, March 15.
T he president was in Palm Beach both days, at his golf club from 8:45 a.m. to 2:37 p.m. on Saturday, and 9:21 a.m. to 1:55 p.m. on Sunday, according to press pool reports. In-person early voting was open from Saturday, March 14 through Sunday, March 22 at 7 p.m. "
Listen, we hate asking for money in every email. Unlike opponents of voting rights, however, there are no secret wealthy donors backing our efforts. There are just our supporters, kicking in $5, $15, or $35 whenever they can. Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
AP: Trump casts Florida mail ballot as he pushes Congress to severely limit that voting option [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=052726_2&amount=25]
Team: Donald Trump voted by mail. No, we're not referring to his well-documented past usage of the practice.
No, after years of attacking vote-by-mail, countless late-night Truth Social rants, and several executive orders within the last year trying to end, or at least curtail, mail-in voting, Donald Trump voted by mail this week, in a Florida special election held on March 24, 2026 . He could have gone to an early voting site when he was at Mar-A-Lago the week before the election, but he chose to submit a mailed ballot instead, according to Palm Beach County voter records.
To be honest, we here at Voter Action Project are glad he did. We believe every eligible American deserves to vote in the manner that is easiest for them to participate. That's because we believe that the act of participation is the most important part, not what method you use to cast your ballot.
It's worth noting, however, how he's very willing to use this tool to help himself and make his own voice heard, but he wants to restrict it for everyone else if it seems like it might not benefit him. The pattern is completely clear, and his self-interest drives every decision and statement he makes about voting.
So next time you run into that anti-voting family member, friend, or neighbor, just let them know: Trump himself chose to skip voting in person while in Florida and voted by mail in 2026.
Onward,
The Voter Action Project Team

subject: Peter, you’re cream of the crop!
body:

| | | | | | 🌵 May 27 Legislative & Campaign Update
Even though we aren’t at the Capitol every day, I’ve continued meeting with constituents and stakeholders and holding important policy calls. Senate and House leadership budget teams are still working with the governor’s office to reach an agreement on the state budget. While several items remain unresolved, we expect negotiations to continue over the next week or two, with the goal of voting on a final budget by mid‐June.🎓 Congratulations to Arizona’s 75,000 high school seniors who walked across the stage this month to receive their diplomas. Your hard work has paid off, and our state is proud of you! 🇺🇸 On Monday, we observed Memorial Day, a national day of profound reverence honoring the U.S. service members who gave their lives in defense of our country. We remember their sacrifice and the families who carry their legacy.Yesterday, I led an online policy discussion via Zoom with Aaron Hedlund, an economist and member of the White House Council of Economic Advisers, who helps drive the administration’s housing‐affordability agenda. I met Aaron last month while I was participating in the spring seminar for The Club for Growth. Members of the Senate and House Republican caucuses joined the conversation. Aaron’s framework focuses on combating housing inflation and supply shortages through targeted deregulation and lowering construction barriers. We also discussed the administration’s broader work on housing affordability and deregulation. One of the bills I have sponsored this session, [Senate Bill 1431](https://bolickforarizona.us7.list-manage.com/track/click?u=3214fdbd528e32d06cf84fc86&id=37c28b4146&e=a7ab36849c), directly addresses these issues the current White House is advocating. SB 1431 updates Arizona law to limit municipal authority over aesthetic design requirements for new homes — such as exterior colors, roof styles, building materials, and other non‐safety‐related features. By streamlining permitting, we can protect private property rights while preserving local authority over essential health, safety, fire, and historic‐district standards. The bill also restricts cities from requiring shared amenities that force the creation of homeowners’ associations unless needed for maintaining common areas. The goal is to bring down housing prices and keep your property rights intact. Over the last twenty years, cities and towns have added layers of “bureaucrat taxes” that drive up costs and reduce much‐needed housing supply.

**Election Integrity & Ballot Measures****** Many constituents have been asking me about ballot propositions related to election integrity, including [SCR 1001](https://bolickforarizona.us7.list-manage.com/track/click?u=3214fdbd528e32d06cf84fc86&id=264eb33e4c&e=a7ab36849c), which I sponsored. The Senate President announced months ago that no ballot referrals would move forward for a vote until the state budget is passed and signed.You may have encountered petition circulators gathering signatures for a union‐backed initiative to change the state’s current Empowerment Scholarship Account (ESA) program, which serves more than 100,000 students. Arizona’s ESA program does not limit who can participate, but the proposed initiative would significantly restrict eligibility and could remove more than 20,000 current families from the program if it qualifies for the ballot and passes. I’ve encouraged individuals who’ve contacted me to decline to sign any ballot initiatives being circulated at this time. Here’s a [link](https://bolickforarizona.us7.list-manage.com/track/click?u=3214fdbd528e32d06cf84fc86&id=3862616645&e=a7ab36849c) to a recent news story discussing this issue.Later this week, I will join Republican state legislators from across the country to discuss school choice and next steps for expanding educational freedom.
📣 **Campaign Update** If you live in District 2, you may have noticed our large campaign signs sprouting up along major intersections across the district. Early voting begins in less than one month, and the primary election will be held on Tuesday, July 21st.**Arizona Nurses Association Endorsed My Primary Election** Last week, I was honored to receive the [Arizona Nurses Association Political Action Committee (AzNA PAC)](https://bolickforarizona.us7.list-manage.com/track/click?u=3214fdbd528e32d06cf84fc86&id=432ad6bf1b&e=a7ab36849c) primary election endorsement. AzNA PAC supports candidates committed to advancing healthcare, improving access to care, protecting public health and safety, and strengthening the nursing profession. As Chair of the Committee on Regulatory Affairs and Government Efficiency, I supported their priority bills they championed to reform the nursing board.**Greater Phoenix Chamber PAC Endorsed My Campaign** Today, the [Greater Phoenix Chamber Political Action Committee](https://bolickforarizona.us7.list-manage.com/track/click?u=3214fdbd528e32d06cf84fc86&id=72e71bb0bb&e=a7ab36849c) released its 2026 primary election endorsements. The Chamber PAC supports candidates who prioritize economic growth, regulatory stability, and a strong business climate.If you live in LD2 and would like to request a yard sign, please request one [HERE](https://bolickforarizona.us7.list-manage.com/track/click?u=3214fdbd528e32d06cf84fc86&id=004b1bfb87&e=a7ab36849c).Thank you for your continued support!Best,Shawnna

Please consider making a financial donation to my campaign to keep our momentum going. If you would like to volunteer, **[**please contact me**](https://bolickforarizona.us7.list-manage.com/track/click?u=3214fdbd528e32d06cf84fc86&id=d51577e7c3&e=a7ab36849c)**.**

The Associated Press called the race for Paxton shortly after 8 p.m., about an hour after most polls closed in Texas.

Paxton’s win, coming on the heels of an eleventh-hour endorsement from President **Donald Trump** , will reverberate nationally. The result is a triumph for Paxton and his wing of the GOP, which prioritizes politicians’ zeal for destroying the left over traditional values like statesmanship and dealmaking. And it’s a massive blow to the Republican old guard in Texas and the political establishment in Washington, who were firmly behind Cornyn amid concerns about Paxton’s electability in November.

The outcome sets up a general election matchup between Paxton and Austin state Rep. **James Talarico**. Democrats have made no secret of their preference for Paxton, who they believe can be beaten due to the baggage he carries from a line of political and personal scandals. Paxton has run and won three times statewide, but Talarico will be by far his best-funded and most prominent opponent, and the first he will face running atop the ticket.

The attorney general received Trump’s backing a week before election day, providing him with a significant boost after both candidates spent a year lobbying for it. Paxton’s victory further demonstrates Trump’s iron grip on his party and the consequences Republicans can face for even mild criticism of a president who demands loyalty. Results below include responses from participants of the Texas Manufacturing Outlook Survey and the Texas Service Sector Outlook Survey. Texas manufacturing output growth decelerated in May, according to business executives responding to the Texas Manufacturing Outlook Survey. The production index, a key measure of state manufacturing conditions, fell 10 points to 9.4, a reading suggestive of an average pace of output expansion. Other measures of manufacturing activity also remained positive but showed signs of slower growth this month. The capacity utilization index plunged 15 points to 5.2, the new orders index dipped four points to 6.4, and the shipments index fell eight points to 7.4. Perceptions of broader business conditions were stable in May. The general business activity index edged up three points to 0.4, with the near-zero reading indicating no change in activity from April. Similarly, the company outlook index came in at 0.3, down from 3.0, with the near-zero May reading signaling no change in outlooks. The outlook uncertainty index was little changed at 19.2, remaining above the series average of 16.9. ( ) » » » “AI takes on big oil’s dirty water problem in the Permian Basin” via ‘s Carlos Nogueras Ramos – Underneath the Permian Basin, the state’s largest oil field, lies an ocean of toxic, unusable wastewater that bursts out of rock formations when oil companies extract fossil fuels from the ground. For years, companies have struggled with how to dispose of it. Now, many are turning to an ubiquitous, albeit controversial, technology to solve the problem — artificial intelligence. In the race to keep up with skyrocketing demand for crude, oil and gas companies are increasingly turning to AI to gain an edge over their competition. ( ) “Fort Worth receives international acclaim for film and TV production boom” via ‘s Brayden Garcia – Film and television production has exploded in Fort Worth over the past few years, and the rest of the world is starting to notice. Since 2015, when the Fort Worth Film Commission was established, the film industry has driven $1 billion in economic impact and created over 50,000 jobs in Cowtown. Several major productions have filmed in the city, including “Landman,” “Lioness” and “Dutton Ranch.” Fort Worth, and the Fort Worth Film Commission, were honored last week with the Emerging Location Award at the Global Production Awards in Cannes, France. “In just 10 years, the Fort Worth Film Commission has grown from a new office to attracting top film and TV projects, like Taylor Sheridan ’s ‘Landman,’ which was the third most-watched original series of 2025,” film commissioner Taylor Hardy said in a statement. “We have worked diligently to strengthen Fort Worth’s film economy and international image; this recognition solidifies our position as a premier production destination.” ( ) “Texas court weighs Infowars net worth as Alex Jones seeks delay” via ‘sPaul Flahive –Alex Jones testifies in August 2022 at the Travis County Courthouse. He and the company he founded are back in state District Court in Austin this week in an attempt to hold off collection of defamation judgments he’s owed since late 2021. Attorneys for the parent company of Infowars and the conspiracy-peddling media platform’s founder Alex Jones are back in state court fighting collection efforts in the case stemming from his lies that the Sandy Hook Elementary School shooting was a government hoax. Jones, who was found liable for defamation after refusing to produce financial documents and comply with other court orders, owes nearly $1.5 billion to the families of the victims of the 2012 mass shooting, whom he called crisis actors in a staged shooting. A hearing Tuesday to determine the net worth of Austin-based Infowars parent company Free Speech Systems LLC marked the latest legal wrangling in the state court case. The company’s value will be used to determine how much Jones should be ordered to pay in a bond to continue an appeal and effectively hold off efforts for his victims to begin collecting on a $50 million judgment in the Texas case. ( ) | 2026 “Ken Paxton defeats John Cornyn for U.S. Senate GOP nomination” via ‘s Gabby Birenbaum , Kayla Guo and Alejandra Martinez – Ken Paxton won the Republican primary runoff for U.S. Senate Tuesday, ending over three decades of Senator John Cornyn’s electoral dominance in what amounts to a watershed moment for GOP politics in Texas. The Associated Press called the race for Paxton shortly after 8 p.m., about an hour after most polls closed in Texas. Paxton’s win, coming on the heels of an eleventh-hour endorsement from President Donald Trump , will reverberate nationally. The result is a triumph for Paxton and his wing of the GOP, which prioritizes politicians’ zeal for destroying the left over traditional values like statesmanship and dealmaking. And it’s a massive blow to the Republican old guard in Texas and the political establishment in Washington, who were firmly behind Cornyn amid concerns about Paxton’s electability in November. The outcome sets up a general election matchup between Paxton and Austin state Rep. James Talarico. Democrats have made no secret of their preference for Paxton, who they believe can be beaten due to the baggage he carries from a line of political and personal scandals. Paxton has run and won three times statewide, but Talarico will be by far his best-funded and most prominent opponent, and the first he will face running atop the ticket. The attorney general received Trump’s backing a week before election day, providing him with a significant boost after both candidates spent a year lobbying for it. Paxton’s victory further demonstrates Trump’s iron grip on his party and the consequences Republicans can face for even mild criticism of a president who demands loyalty. And it sends a chilling message to the Republican establishment, which has now lost one of its most powerful senators and best fundraisers. ( ) ““The last of the gentlemen Republicans”: John Cornyn’s four-decade political career ends with a MAGA uprising” via ‘sKayla Guo – The beginning of the end for John Cornyn came in 2022, when he was doing the thing he was once praised for: whipping votes to pass difficult, bipartisan legislation. That year, moved by the Uvalde school shooting, Texas’ senior senator convinced 14 Senate Republicans to buck the National Rifle Association and join him in passing the most significant gun safety bill in a generation. “This was fundamentally important to the country at a time when things are so polarized and people are so intolerant of others that have different points of view,” he said after it passed. “I thought it was important to demonstrate the Senate could work.” It was legacy defining, but not in the way he had hoped. Later that year, he was booed at the Texas GOP convention for an agonizing 45 seconds straight before he even began his remarks. When he launched into his speech, packed full of red meat, the jeers did not stop. ( ) “Mayes Middleton wins the Republican primary runoff for Texas attorney general” via ‘s Harrison Mantas – State Sen. Mayes Middleton defeated U.S. Rep.Chip Roy in the Republican Party primary runoff for Texas attorney general, according to the Associated Press. He will now face Democratic State Sen. Nathan Johnson in the Nov. 3 General election to determine who will succeed incumbent Attorney General Ken Paxton , who is projected to win his runoff against four-term incumbent U.S. Senate incumbent John Cornyn for the Republican nomination. This is the first election since 2015 without an incumbent running to be Texas’s highest ranking prosecutor. Chip Roy acknowledged the results in a post on X. “Just a little while ago, I called and congratulated @mayesmiddleton for his victory in our race for the Republican nominee for Attorney General. I will have a full statement tomorrow. Onward,” Roy posted. ( ) “Bo French defeats Railroad Commissioner Jim Wright in GOP primary runoff” via Texas Tribune’sCarlos Nogeuras Ramos – Bo French defeated Railroad CommissionerJim Wright in the primary runoff Tuesday night, prevailing in a campaign where French prioritized issues like fighting DEI and Sharia Law over traditional regulatory issues. French will face Democratic state Rep. Jon Rosenthal in the November general election. A Democrat has not held a seat on the railroad commission in decades. “I am deeply grateful for the support of TX Republicans across our state. Our campaign focused on defending oil and gas, and putting America First—and that’s exactly what I will continue fighting for as we turn our attention to radical Democrat Jon Rosenthal,” French said in a social media post. The race for the typically under-the-radar office emerged on Tuesday as one of the closest contests of the night, with French leading with early voters but Wright narrowing the gap as the Election Day vote trickled in. If he wins in November, he will join the three-commissioner panel presiding over the railroad commission, a century-old regulatory institution tasked with overseeing the state’s oil and gas industry, an immense enterprise that produced nearly half of all U.S. oil last year. A former Tarrant County GOP chairman, French espouses some of the most extreme views among Texas Republican officials, even as the party has pivoted further to the right in recent years. Earlier this year, said the U.S. should deport 100 million people, nearly a third of the country’s population and a number that suggests he wants to deport U.S. citizens. () “Goodwin defeated Marcos Vélez and in November will face Lt. Gov.” via Texas Tribune’s Alejandro Serrano – State Rep. Vikki Goodwin of Austin won a runoff election to be the Democratic nominee for lieutenant governor, beating a Houston labor leader and first-time candidate who had indirectly received support from the party’s top campaign partner and racked up a variety of endorsements. Dan Patrick , the popular GOP leader who is sitting on more than $30 million in his campaign coffers and won his own primary in March by the widest margin since he became the state’s second-highest executive 11 years ago. “Tonight, Texans chose a politics rooted in decency, dignity, and the belief that our state belongs to all of us,” Goodwin . “Now, we keep going, for public schools, affordable housing, accessible healthcare, clean water, and a Texas that is kinder, safer, and more hopeful.” Goodwin and Vélez advanced to the runoff after neither secured more than 50% of the vote during the March primary. On the campaign trail, Goodwin pitched herself to voters as a public schools advocate who will also fight for affordability, healthcare access and water infrastructure. Vélez, meanwhile, as a blue collar union leader who has a finger on the pulse of a working class that wants a lieutenant governor focused on affordability. Goodwin will face an uphill battle to unseat Patrick, a of President Donald Trump who has steadily pushed the Texas Senate, which he presides over, ever to the right. Most of the job’s authorities are derived from the rules passed by senators at the beginning of each legislative session. () “Colin Allred tops Julie Johnson in redistricting-driven runoff battle of Dallas Democrats” via Texas Tribune’s Olivia Borgula – Former Rep. Colin Allred defeated his successor in Congress, Rep.Julie Johnson , in the Democratic runoff to represent Texas’ Dallas-centered congressional district, according to the Associated Press. The Democrats were forced into an unusual race between predecessor and successor after Republicans redrew Texas’ district map to boost GOP chances to maintain congressional control. The 32nd District, which Johnson currently represents and Allred previously represented, is now solidly Republican, pushing Johnson into the left-leaning 33rd District that Kamala Harris would have won by more than 30 points — had its boundaries existed in 2024. District 33 contains about a third of the residents from the candidates’ former congressional district and is currently represented by Rep. Marc Veasey , who decided not to seek reelection. Allred, a civil rights lawyer and former professional football player, first served in Congress from 2019 to 2025 after unseating 11-term Republican Pete Sessions. He left his seat to run for Senate against Ted Cruz and lost decisively in the 2024 midterms. () “Tom Sell, Jon Bonck win open GOP primary runoffs for solidly red congressional seats” via Texas Tribune’s Ayden Runnels – RepublicansTom Sell and Jon Bonck won their primary runoffs Tuesday for a pair of open congressional seats in Texas’ South Plains and the Houston area, respectively, making them the heavy favorites to join the U.S. House next year representing the deep red districts. Republican voters in Texas’ , which represents a wedge of West Texas from Lubbock to Abilene, elected Sell as the Republican nominee. Sell, a businessman with deep familial ties to Lubbock, was endorsed by several U.S. House GOP leaders, including House Majority Leader Steve Scalise and House Majority Whip Tom Emmer. PresidentDonald Trump won by a 52-point margin in the 19th Congressional District during the 2024 presidential election, his widest in the state. Sell’s opponent in the runoff, Abraham Enriquez, made his support for Trump a of his unsuccessful bid for the seat. Trump did not endorse either candidate in the district, but Gov. Greg Abbott and Lt. Gov. Dan Patrick both threw behind Enriquez, with Patrick describing Enriquez as “the true America First conservative in this race.” The seat opened up after Rep.Jodey Arrington , R-Lubbock, who served in the district since 2017 and chairs the U.S. House Budget Committee, in November that he would retire. Trump had endorsed Arrington in his 2020 and 2024 reelection campaigns. () “Rep. Al Green defeated by freshman Rep. Christian Menefee in a generational primary runoff contest” via AP – In a generational contest between sitting congressmen, freshman Rep.Christian Menefee defeated veteran Rep. Al Green in a Democratic primary runoff for a Houston-area district created last year by an unusual Republican-led redistricting effort. Green, known for his protests during President Donald Trump’s speeches, has served in Congress since 2005. He became a standard-bearer of progressive legislation on racial justice, often drawing the ire of Republicans. “I am so honored to have served for these many years, more than twenty. And I’m honored to have done some things that I’m very proud of,” Green told his supporters during an election night event. “You probably see me smiling and it’s because it’s because this is not the end,” he added as the audience cheered. “This is the beginning of a new chapter.” () “Luz Elena Chapa wins tight runoff for Bexar County DA” via ‘sSaul Pink and Megan Rodriguez –Luz Elena Chapa , a former appellate court justice who campaigned on bringing an outside perspective to Bexar County’s top prosecutor job, won the Democratic nomination for Bexar County district attorney Tuesday night. She narrowly beat Jane Davis , a career prosecutor who currently runs the office’s juvenile division and argued that Chapa was far too inexperienced for the job. Chapa carried 51% of the vote. She led by nearly 1,000 votes late Tuesday night with 86% of precincts reporting their totals. “I look forward to carrying the Democratic Party banner in November and being Bexar County’s next District Attorney,” Chapa said in a statement Tuesday night. A representative for Davis’ campaign said she’s still processing the results and did not immediately comment on the outcome. ( ) | STATE GOVERNMENT “Texas could require hunters to report mountain lion kills under new state rules” via ‘s Liz Teitz – Texas wildlife regulators are weighing new rules that would require anyone who kills a mountain lion to report it to the state within 24 hours. State regulators will decide this week whether to approve new rules for mountain lion harvesting, aimed at learning more about the species’ population in Texas. Mountain lions, also known as cougars and pumas, are considered “nongame” animals in Texas, meaning there are no limits on when they can be hunted or trapped on private property. Texas Parks and Wildlife commissioners are scheduled to vote Thursday on new rules that wouldn’t change that, but would require anyone who kills a mountain lion to report it to the state. ( ) | LOCAL GOVERNMENT “Bexar County officials give go-ahead to tax break for H-E-B expansion” via ‘s Madison Iszler – H-E-B wants to expand its manufacturing and distribution facilities off of South Foster Road on San Antonio’s East Side. Bexar County Commissioners Court unanimously gave the go-ahead Tuesday to county staff to negotiate a $15 million tax break for H-E-B’s proposed $700 million expansion of its distribution operations on San Antonio’s East Side. The San Antonio company wants to add a bakery, refrigerated warehouse and building for returned goods to its cluster of facilities along South Foster Road and south of East Houston Street. H-E-B is making its largest-ever investment in its manufacturing and supply chain operations as the company opens more stores and makes more of its own products. “This is a project of magnitude we have not had in our supply chain before,” Ben Scott , group vice president of real estate at H-E-B, told commissioners. ( ) “North Texas cities take transit into their own hands with new rideshare programs” via ‘s Pablo Arauz Peña – Several North Texas cities are turning to rideshare programs to supplement – or replace – public transit. The programs work like other rideshare services like Uber or Lyft but are city-funded. Earlier this month, Plano, Addison, Highland Park and Frisco launched their programs in partnership with microtransit company Via. Moniah Dailey , communications specialist with the city of Plano, said her city’s new pilot program for seniors 65 and older is performing better than expected just a few weeks after launch. “We are kind of ahead of where I think we were going to be,” Dailey told KERA. Since it began on May 4, the new service, called Plano Rides, has completed more than 1,500 rides. The new app linked to the service has been downloaded more than 1,300 times. “For this service and it being like a niche demographic, yeah, that’s pretty successful,” Dailey said. Currently, the Plano Rides service is free until June 4. After that, it’ll be $3 per ride, which is the average cost for the service in other North Texas cities. ( ) | BUSINESS NEWS “SpaceX wins major Space Force contract ahead of planned IPO” via ‘s Brandon Lingle – A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket is seen lifting off from the Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in late 2023. The rocket was carrying 23 Starlink satellites. SpaceX on Tuesday received a $2.29 billion contract from the Space Force to build a military satellite network for communications and the “Golden Dome” missile defense system. SpaceX has landed a $2.29 billion deal with the U.S. Space Force to build a satellite network for military communications and President Donald Trump ’s “Golden Dome” missile defense project. The contract, which appears to be the largest military satellite contract to date for Elon Musk ’s space firm, comes weeks before the Starbase-based company is set to go public in what could be the largest-ever initial public offering. The work will likely go to SpaceX subsidiary Starlink, which provides satellite internet service around the world and is the company’s biggest moneymaker. Starlink already operates Starshield, a secure network for the U.S. government and military. ( ) “First look: Demolition starts for AT &T;’s new billion-dollar Plano campus” via ‘s Nick Wooten – One of North Texas’ most high-profile development projects has reached an important initial milestone. Crews began demolishing the driveway and north parking garage at 5400 Legacy Drive last week, making way for the new billion-dollar-plus headquarters that AT&T; plans to build in Plano. By Friday, excavators were picking through concrete rubble. AT&T; and project developer KDC have offered few details about the project and its timeline, but Plano Deputy City Manager Doug McDonald said larger buildings will come down in the near future. Full demolition could take five to six months, he said. The property was once the headquarters of Electronic Data Systems headquarters, H. Ross Perot Sr. ’s information technology company that was founded in the 1960s. ( ) “Inside the yearslong Texas Disposal Systems courtroom fight that split a family” via ‘s Paul Flahive – The Central Texas trash company the two brothers founded 50 years ago has grown into one of the nation’s largest independently owned waste management companies. It now reaps tens of millions of dollars in profit — but has torn their family apart. Allegations of self-dealing, greed, stolen confidential business records and a behind-the-scenes sale attempt permeate more than 500 court filings in a court saga that has spanned four years. This month, a jury found that one of the brothers and the companies they owned deserve a $116 million payout. “I think the jury felt sad for both brothers, but their verdict was very clear that they believed that Bobby Gregory didn’t do right by the companies that the brothers owned together,” said attorney Casey Dobson , who represents Jimmy Gregory. ( ) “Defense startup to relocate HQ to Cedar Park, hire 135 new workers” via ‘s Karoline Leonard – Aeon Industrial Inc., an Austin-based defense startup, plans to double its workforce as it moves its headquarters to Cedar Park. Aeon Industrial plans to build a 48,000-square-foot facility on a vacant lot in Cedar Park next door to Firefly Aerospace Inc.’s new headquarters, according to Cedar Park city documents. “We’re making this move because demand has outpaced our current production capacity,” CEO and Founder Naweed Tahmas said. Cedar Park City Council will vote on an economic development agreement this week to support Aeon Industrial’s new headquarters and manufacturing facility, which will represent a total investment of $8.5 million and the creation of at least 135 new jobs. #
Peter, I’ve been on the road on my Whiteboard Warriors Tour, hosting town halls across the state—and I want to share exactly what I’ve been hearing.
**No matter where I go, the message is the same: working people are just stretched too thin. They’re doing everything right, and _still_ falling behind.**
I’ve talked to parents working full-time who still can’t afford child care. Small business owners who are barely hanging on while big corporations rake in record profits. Families watching their budgets tighten every month as rent keeps going up.
These are real problems happening in every corner of our state, and they won’t be solved by politicians who don’t live them.
I’m a single mom. I’ve had to budget every dollar, struggle to make cuts, and figure out how to make it all work. And I’ll tell you this: _the people in charge right now aren’t feeling that pressure—but they should be._
I’m running for governor to put working Californians first and tackle the affordability crisis head-on. That means single-payer health care, free child care, less expensive housing, and more.
**This tour is about more than just sharing my plan. It’s how I hear directly from Californians and fight to make these solutions real.**
And I’m doing it without taking a single penny from corporate PACs—because we deserve a governor who isn’t owned by billionaires or special interests.

body:
| Friend,

I’ve spent enough time in politics to know this: when Democrats stop showing up in certain places, somebody else fills the void.

Usually, it’s people who have no real interest in helping working families — just dividing them, distracting them, and cashing in while communities get left behind. After a while, that kind of politics takes a toll. People start feeling like nobody sees them, nobody hears them, and nobody is fighting for the places they call home.

_I think there’s a better path._

It starts by taking small towns seriously. It starts by respecting people enough to tell the truth. And it starts by showing up, organizing, and competing in places too many folks in politics have given up on. **That’s a big part of why I’m launching Small Town PAC.**

Small Town PAC is about helping Democrats expand the map by building power in small towns and backing the kind of politics that actually speak to working families. Because if we want to win in more places, we’ve got to be willing to show up in more places.

That’s the work ahead, and I’m asking you to be part of it from the start.

[If you’re able, please split a donation between Small Town PAC and the Voter Protection Project to become a founding donor today. They’re pouring **MILLIONS** into my race every day to try and obliterate me this midterm.

# Every American Should _Unlock_ Their IRA/401k In 2026
---
|
---
| | Most Americans have no idea their Retirement Plan is _locked down_.
---
---
Let’s say you’re at a restaurant -- you can order anything you want, as long as it’s on the menu. But what if you found out you have a fish allergy, and you’re at a seafood restaurant? Because if you’ve had an employer 401(k), then you remember seeing the options: You can invest in anything you want, as long as it’s on the menu. Same thing with many IRA plans.
---
**But what happens if**** _everything on the menu_****can make you sick?** That’s what many Americans are facing right now. Because whether you order the S&P Index Fund, the 60/40 Stocks and Bonds mix, or any other combination on the menu... All the ingredients come from the same kitchen -- the stock market. **And you already know the stock market has made people**** _sick_****.****** The ups and downs can be nauseating. Now that’s _not_ a problem if you’re a few decades away from retirement, because you can ride out the storm, and things could likely turn in your favor. **But when you’re already retired, or about to retire, then the game changes.** Because it’s not about growing your assets anymore, it’s about _preserving_ your assets, right? That means if you have $1 million saved for retirement... Then you expect that million to pay for your travel, gifts, visits to family and grandkids... For the rest of your life. Literally! And that’s a great plan.
---
---
---
So how do you tackle the problem? You could hope the stock market rockets up again, and grows your retirement... **[Or you could look at assets that help defend against inflation.](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)** Except the problem is, many IRAs and 401(k)s can be _locked out_ of inflation-defending assets. But it doesn’t have to be that way. Because right now, **_thousands of Americans_** have figured out how to **_UNLOCK_** their IRA/401(k) so they can diversify a portion of their retirement savings into assets that help defend against inflation.
---
[**That’s why we put together this free guide.**](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.) It’s a brief, to-the-point handbook that shows you:
---
* **The IRS Rule That Lets You Access Locked Retirement Funds**
* **Who _Really_ Controls Your Retirement Savings**
* **How To Transition To An Unlocked IRA**

---
| | [](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
And it’s completely free to get a copy. So what you do with your retirement savings is your business, but at the very least, you should be educated about your options. But of course, the choice is yours.
---
[**GET YOUR FREE GUIDE THAT UNLOCKS YOUR IRA/401(k)**](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
